newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Canada's Thiessen sees room for growth.
newsitem.headline: Bank Canada's Thiessen sees room for growth.

text.p: Bank of Governor Gordon Thiessen said on Friday that there was room for growth in jobs and output without spurring inflation.

"The Canadian economy should have room for strong above-potential rates of growth in output and employment in coming quarters without a resurgence of inflation," Thiessen said in a speech to economists.

Thiessen said Canada's high unemployment was a concern but that he expected economic growth to lead to a boost in private sector job growth and in consumer confidence in 1997. Canada's unemployment has been at 9.7 percent for the past few months.
Thiessen said that he expected Canada's strong growth would mean that "the margin of unused capacity in our economy will shrink substantially over the next couple of years."
He repeated that the central bank would maintain its policy of targeting inflation in the one to three percent range.
